subject: history
topicDisplay: Depth Study South Africa C1940 C1994
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which 1950 law forced different racial groups to live in separate designated areas?
options: The Reservation of Separate Amenities Act
questions.explain: The Group Areas Act of 1950 segregated residential areas by race.

questions.q: At which 1964 trial was Nelson Mandela sentenced to life imprisonment?
questions.explain: The Rivonia Trial (1963-64) led to Mandela's life sentence.

questions.q: Roughly how many people were killed when police fired on protesters at Sharpeville in 1960?
questions.explain: Police killed 69 people, many shot in the back, at Sharpeville in March 1960.

questions.q: What Afrikaans word literally meaning 'apartness' described the system of racial segregation?
questions.explain: 'Apartheid' means 'apartness' or 'separateness' in Afrikaans.

questions.q: In which year was Nelson Mandela released from prison?
questions.explain: Nelson Mandela was released on 11 February 1990.

questions.q: Which 1955 gathering of anti-apartheid groups adopted the Freedom Charter?
questions.explain: The Congress of the People at Kliptown in 1955 adopted the Freedom Charter demanding equal rights.

questions.q: Which year saw the National Party come to power and begin formally building the apartheid system?
questions.explain: The National Party won the 1948 election and began legislating apartheid that year.

questions.q: Who was the last apartheid-era president, who freed Mandela and negotiated reforms?
questions.explain: F.W. de Klerk released Mandela and helped end apartheid.

questions.q: Which Anglican archbishop won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1984 for opposing apartheid peacefully?
questions.explain: Archbishop Desmond Tutu won the 1984 Nobel Peace Prize for his anti-apartheid campaign.

questions.q: Which National Party leader is often called the 'architect of apartheid'?
questions.explain: Hendrik Verwoerd, Prime Minister from 1958, was the chief architect of apartheid.

questions.q: In which year did the Sharpeville Massacre, in which police killed 69 protesters, take place?
questions.explain: The Sharpeville Massacre occurred on 21 March 1960.

questions.q: The ANC's militant wing, formed in 1961 after Sharpeville, was known by what name?
options: Umkhonto we Sizwe (Spear of the Nation)
questions.explain: Umkhonto we Sizwe, the ANC's armed wing, was formed in 1961.

questions.q: Which 1953 law deliberately gave black South Africans an inferior schooling?
questions.explain: The 1953 Bantu Education Act provided deliberately inferior schooling for black children.

questions.q: International pressure on apartheid increasingly took the form of economic what from the 1980s?
questions.explain: Economic sanctions and boycotts increasingly isolated apartheid South Africa in the 1980s.

questions.q: In which year were South Africa's first multiracial democratic elections held?
questions.explain: The first fully democratic elections were held in 1994, making Mandela president.

questions.q: Documents that black South Africans were forced to carry to control their movement were called what?
questions.explain: The pass laws required black South Africans to carry passbooks.

questions.q: Which liberation movement led by Mandela launched its armed struggle with sabotage attacks from 1961?
questions.explain: The ANC, through its wing Umkhonto we Sizwe, began sabotage in 1961 after peaceful protest was banned.

questions.q: In which year did Nelson Mandela become South Africa's first black president following all-race elections?
questions.explain: Mandela won the first multiracial elections and became president in 1994.

questions.q: Which organisation, with Mandela among its leaders, was the main movement opposing apartheid?
questions.explain: The African National Congress led the struggle against apartheid.

questions.q: In which year did South Africa become a republic and leave the Commonwealth amid apartheid criticism?
questions.explain: South Africa became a republic and left the Commonwealth in 1961.

questions.q: In which year was the ANC banned by the South African government following Sharpeville?
questions.explain: The ANC was banned in 1960 in the aftermath of the Sharpeville Massacre.

questions.q: Which 1950 law classified every South African by racial group?
questions.explain: The Population Registration Act of 1950 classified people by race.
